answer: A time-locked bond protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to deposit escrowed collateral before registering. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of illiquid capital per active persona. For instance, an agent operating from an island haven must lock funds before managing transport across a lagoon jetty. This financial commitment prevents cheap identity duplication. However, capital bonding inherently favors wealthy entities and excludes underfunded participants.
